subject: Re: Dedicated capacity demo — throughput & latency planning
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel@opentide.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia@opentide.io>
Date: Sun, 14 Jul 2029 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Dedicated capacity demo for OpenTide — high throughput

Hi Ben,

We self-signed up and kicked the tires on Redwood last week (thanks for the great docs). We're evaluating Dedicated capacity for a production inference tier and would like a focused demo that covers throughput and latency guarantees, networking/VPC setup, and an ops runbook.

High-level constraints:
- Peak concurrency: ~600 concurrent requests (burst to 1k for short windows)
- Target p95 latency: < 150 ms for 256-token requests
- Typical request size: 120-300 tokens, average ~180 tokens
- Model patterns: mix of generation with streaming and embedding calls for routing

Can you set up a 30–45 minute call this week with an ops/solutions engineer to validate capacity sizing and show a short perf run? I've attached our SLA requirements and a simplified network diagram.

Attachments: opentide_sla_requirements.pdf (PDF, 420 KB); network_topology.png (PNG, 150 KB)

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Director of Platform Engineering
OpenTide Analytics
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Hi Daniel — thanks for the details and the attachments. Really helpful.

We can absolutely walk through Dedicated capacity sizing and run a short perf sweep. Quick asks so we make the session productive:
- Do you have a preferred time window (we work across PT/ET)?
- Is the 600 concurrent number steady-state or a burst profile?
- Would you like a live perf run against a sandbox model or a slides-first discussion?

I've looped in Sofia (solutions/ops) and Marissa (AM) to join the call — Sofia can drive the perf sizing and the VPC/network guidance. Book a 30–45 min slot here if that helps: https://cal.new/ben/rdw-demo-30

If you prefer, propose a few times and we will confirm.

Best,
Ben Carter | Senior SDR, Redwood Inference

Hi Ben / Sofia —

Thanks — booking link works. We're leaning toward a live perf run so we can validate p95 numbers. The concurrency is a steady-state of ~600 with occasional bursts to 1k for 3–5 minute windows. We use 2–3 different prompt templates; I'll attach a sanitized sample prompt set if that helps.

Can you do Thursday 10:00 AM PT (July 18) for 45 minutes? Procurement may join for a short segment at the end.

I'll upload a small sample prompt set to the Drive link if you confirm.

Best,

Thanks Daniel — Thursday 10:00 AM PT works for us. Confirmed: July 18, 10:00 AM PT / 1:00 PM ET, 45 minutes. I've added a short pre-call checklist so we can size correctly and use the time for the perf run:

Pre-call checklist (please provide before Tue 16 Jul, 5pm PT if possible):
- Representative sample traffic: 300–500 anonymized requests with token counts and timestamps (CSV or JSON).
- Distribution of seq lengths (min/median/p95) and concurrency over a typical 1-hour window.
- Are embeddings routed to a different path? If yes, approximate % of requests that are embeddings.
- Any enforced safety filters or post-processing that adds CPU overhead.
- Network egress requirements and VPC peering expectations (we saw your topology but need specifics on CIDR and NAT).
- Region preference (we can run in us-west-2 or us-east-1).

If you prefer, we can run a short pre-demo perf sweep on our side using your sample prompts (anonymized). That helps us come to the call with concrete GPU pool sizing and a proposed quantization profile.

Call agenda (45 minutes):
1) Quick intros (5m) — OpenTide + Redwood ops
2) Runbook & architecture review (10m)
3) Live perf sweep with 3 concurrency points (20m)
4) Sizing recommendation, bill-of-materials, and next steps (10m)

Related links: HS-238412 (HubSpot), shared Drive folder (https://drive.redwood.example/rdw/ops-handbook).

I've attached a short ops checklist PDF for your procurement team to preview.

Attachments: rdw_pre_demo_checklist.pdf (PDF, 85 KB)

Looking forward — Sofia Ivanova
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
